context: rotating-equipment-led · chemical recovery cycle drives wet-end start-up

brief.intro: A pulp & paper mill turns wood chips or pulp into paper: chemical or mechanical pulping, chemical recovery, then forming, pressing, drying and winding on a paper machine. The programme is dominated by heavy rotating equipment — digesters, refiners and the paper machine's long roll train — set on precision foundations, plus steam/condensate and chemical recovery (black-liquor) systems that must be proven before the wet end can run. Because a paper machine runs at high speed with tight alignment tolerances, mechanical completion of the roll train and drive train is its own discipline, distinct from ordinary piping and electrical work. The critical path runs through long-lead process equipment — digesters, headbox, dryer cans, recovery boiler — into precision alignment, steam-up and the first reel, with the chemical recovery cycle (recovery boiler, evaporators, causticizing) forming a parallel, equally long chain. Both chains have to land together, or the later one dictates the start-up date.

must_get_right: Order and align the paper machine roll train early — precision alignment (not just power) determines run speed and quality, and it cannot be rushed at the end.

Sequence the chemical recovery cycle (recovery boiler, evaporators, causticizing) in parallel with the fibre line — mechanical completion of one without the other stalls chemical self-sufficiency and wet-end start-up.
Protect steam-up and mechanical run-in time before wet-end start-up — bearings, drives and dryer cans need supervised run-in under load before the first reel.
Treat recovery-boiler pressure-part work as code-inspected work with formal hold points, not as ordinary structural steel.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities carry durations in working days; the network is calculated (F9) with no artificial constraints beyond contractual milestones. Total float is kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and structural steel run a 6-day week; mechanical/piping erection around the digester, recovery boiler and paper machine moves to two shifts at peak to protect the critical path; commissioning (steam-up, run-in) runs a continuous 7-day calendar once started, since a partial shutdown mid-sequence is costly to recover from. A weather allowance is embedded in the civil calendar.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Two parallel driving chains converge at wet-end start-up: (1) the chemical recovery cycle — digester → evaporators → recovery boiler (pressure-part code inspection) → causticizing/lime kiln — which must reach chemical self-sufficiency before sustained production; and (2) the paper machine — foundations → roll-train set → precision alignment → drive coupling → steam-up → mechanical run-in. Whichever chain finishes later drives the first-reel date; both are tracked as co-critical, not sequential.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design of process equipment — digester, recovery boiler, paper machine configuration — is frozen before ordering; a single mobilisation; existing fibre supply/wood-yard arrangements are in place; and no late change to basis weight or grade range that would alter the paper machine's forming/dryer configuration.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Heavy lifts — digester shells, recovery-boiler drum, dryer cans, headbox — require crane capacity and clear rigging access inside the machine hall, in some cases before the roof closes. Alignment work on the roll train needs a dust-controlled, temperature-stable environment. Skilled millwrights for precision alignment are a scarce, shared resource late in the programme.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: recovery-boiler pressure-part inspection delays, roll-train misalignment discovered only at run-in, and chemical-recovery-cycle commissioning issues that push back wet-end start-up. Schedule contingency is held before mechanical run-in and before the first-reel milestone rather than spread across erection activities.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
